Subject: NimbleWare pilot — post-demo pricing & throughput clarifications

Hi Liam — great demo earlier, thanks for the time. Quick recap + a couple of clarifying questions so we can size a pilot/quote: 

Recap (from today's call)
- Goal: move from R&D PoC to a 3-month pilot supporting smart search + document summarization across ~200 internal users.
- Expected traffic: mostly internal developer/testing for first 6 weeks, then broader usage.
- Target latency SLO: ~300ms tail for short prompts; acceptable ~500ms for long-generation flows.

Clarifying questions (to confirm for capacity sizing / unit econ):
1) Monthly token estimate: you mentioned 4–6M tokens/day on average — can you confirm a realistic monthly baseline and a peak-day multiplier (x1.5, x2, etc.)?
2) Average generation length per request (tokens generated, not input) — you said some summaries are ~350 tokens; can you give a 50th/90th percentile if available?
3) Peak concurrency / qps during your busiest hour (approx requests/sec or concurrent sessions).
4) Budget range for dedicated/reserved capacity vs. short pilot (ballpark $/month or $/1M tokens target).

Budget anchor helps a lot when we decide GPU family (A100 vs H100) and how many lanes to reserve. Attached a quick token-modeling sheet I started (nimbleware_token_modeling.xlsx) — if you can drop numbers there I'll run a pricing sketch.

Next steps I propose:
- You answer the above 1–4 (quick reply).
- We propose 2 pilot configs (lower-cost A100 baseline, higher-throughput H100 baseline) with $/1M token anchors and expected monthly invoice.
- Security questionnaire + pilot data scope (we'll kick off with our solutions engineer).

If easier, feel free to put rough numbers in the sheet and send back. I can produce a 1-page pilot option by EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Diego
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Diego — thanks, this is great. Quick answers inline and I've updated the sheet with the numbers we discussed.

1) Monthly tokens: baseline ~150M tokens/month (avg 5M/day). Peak day we expect ~1.8x baseline (we had a few heavy annotation-days in the PoC).
2) Generation length: median ~120 tokens, 90th ~420 tokens (summaries vary; search responses shorter ~40–80).
3) Peak concurrency: busiest hour ~20 concurrent requests, peaks at ~6–8 rps for the long-running summarization jobs.
4) Budget: for pilot we'd like to keep committed spend under $3k/month if possible — long term we'd target <$6 per 1M tokens but open to a higher pilot anchor if it lowers latency.

On GPU preference: engineering prefers H100 if price delta is reasonable because of latency for our long summaries.

We can sign an NDA/SLA and provide sample data once we have a pilot scope. Sara (cc) will coordinate security/engineering follow-ups.

—Liam

Thanks Liam — appreciated. Based on your numbers I sketched two pilot configurations (high level):

Pilot A (cost-focused)
- Hardware: 1x A100-80GB reserved lane
- Expected sustained throughput: ~800–1,200 tokens/sec (suitable for 5M tokens/day baseline with modest burst headroom)
- Latency: expected median <400ms for short responses, tails up to ~700ms for longer summaries
- Pricing anchor (pilot, month-to-month): $8.50 per 1M tokens => ~ $1,275/month on 150M tokens (non-committed).

Pilot B (latency-focused)
- Hardware: 1x H100-equivalent reserved lane (or 2x scaled A100 config)
- Expected sustained throughput: ~2,500 tokens/sec with 2–3x burst capability (handles 1.8x peak-day without queuing)
- Latency: median <250ms for short prompts, tails ~350–450ms for long summaries
- Pricing anchor (pilot, month-to-month): $12.00 per 1M tokens => ~ $1,800/month on 150M tokens (non-committed).

Commit discounts & path to unit econ
- 6–12 month commitment can reduce unit price materially. Example: 12-month committed seat on Pilot B reduces to ~$6.25 per 1M tokens in our model (assuming reserved lanes + committed throughput). Exact numbers depend on lane-count and quantization choices.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Confirm whether you want to pursue Pilot A (cost) or Pilot B (latency).
2) If Pilot B, confirm H100 preference — we'll price both an H100 lane and an equivalent A100 scaled config.
3) We'll prepare a 1-page commercial: monthly estimated invoice, $/1M token anchor, and a short rollout plan + security kickoff.
4) Legal/security: if you can share a primary contact (Sara is great) we'll send the minimal pilot-level DPA + SOC checklist.

I've attached a one-page draft terms doc (redwood-pilot-terms-draft.pdf) and updated the modeling sheet with the two pilots. If you confirm Pilot B and H100 today we can get a pilot account up within 3 business days.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 20-min call to align.

Diego
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
